### Observed differences

- The mix of successors chosen after A21 shifted between the windows. In the earlier window, among A21's observed outgoing transitions, roughly 31 in 100 went to A23 and about 27 in 100 to A25, while A24 received about 17 in 100. In the later window, A24 received about 26 in 100, A23 about 21 in 100 and A25 about 20 in 100, with smaller rises for A17 (about 3 to 7 in 100), A19 (about 13 to 17 in 100) and A20 (about 1 to 2 in 100). The overall profile difference was about 0.07 on the indicator's cosine scale and was larger than about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits of the pooled traces, based on 200 observed outgoing transitions of A21 in each window [DIR001].

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. The control-flow family produced one qualifying item where about 0.3 would be expected by chance in an unchanged process, so a single routing difference at A21 — even one larger than about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits — is within what a stable process typically produces, and no participation or ordering evidence is available to corroborate it [DIR001].

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

The evidence contains:
- 200 traces before, 200 traces after
- Screening: 73 units tested, 0.3 items expected without change overall
  - Control flow: 59 units tested, 1 item, 0.29 expected without change
  - Time: 14 units tested, 0 items, 0.007 expected

Evidence items: only one, DIR001.

DIR001: CF_DIR indicator on activity A21. It's about outgoing transitions of A21 — the distribution of successors of A21. The profile before: A23: 0.31, A15: 0.055, A19: 0.13, A24: 0.165, A25: 0.27, A16: 0.035, A20: 0.005, A17: 0.03. After: A24: 0.26, A16: 0.035, A15: 0.055, A19: 0.165, A23: 0.205, A17: 0.07, A20: 0.015, A25: 0.195.

So the outgoing transition shares of A21 shifted: A23 dropped from about 31% to about 20.5% of A21's outgoing transitions, A25 dropped from 27% to 19.5%, while A24 rose from 16.5% to 26%, A17 from 3% to 7%, A19 from 13% to 16.5%, A20 from 0.5% to 1.5%.

Observed change: 0.0677 (cosine dissimilarity). Empirical strength: 0.995 — the difference is larger than in about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits. Support: 200 outgoing transitions observed in each window (well, support before 200, after 200 — for DIR, support is outgoing transitions of the source activity).

Now the judgement: The screening comparison. Control flow family: 1 item vs 0.29 expected. Per the instructions: "A count of the same order as that expectation (for example one or two items when fewer than one is expected) is what an unchanged process typically produces: choose 'Insufficient evidence', however large or unusual a single item looks."

Here we have 1 control-flow item when 0.29 are expected. That's the same order as the expectation (one item when fewer than one is expected). So per the rules, this is "Insufficient evidence".

Time family: 0 items vs 0.007 expected — nothing there.

So the verdict is Insufficient evidence. The single DIR item, though it has high empirical strength (0.995), is exactly what an unchanged process produces occasionally (1 item vs 0.29 expected — about 3.4x, but the rule says "one or two items when fewer than one is expected" is what an unchanged process typically produces). Hmm, let me re-read: "A count of the same order as that expectation (for example one or two items when fewer than one is expected) is what an unchanged process typically produces: choose 'Insufficient evidence', however large or unusual a single item looks."

Yes — 1 item when 0.29 expected falls under this. So Insufficient evidence.

Also, the DIR item alone is a routing-share shift at A21's outgoing transitions. But even if we considered it, a shift in path frequencies requires that every activity and path involved is observed in a substantial share of traces in both windows. The DIR shares are over outgoing transitions, not cases. The changes are moderate: A23 from ~31% to ~20.5% of A21's outgoing transitions, A24 from ~16.5% to ~26%. But we don't have participation evidence (OCC) showing these successors are in substantial shares of traces. So we can't fully verify the condition. But the primary reason is the screening count.

Also note: no time or resource items in the evidence (only DIR001, control flow). The screening mentions a time family with 0 items, but the evidence list contains no TWAIT items. The instruction says "Do not discuss time or resources when the evidence contains no such items." The screening by_family includes time, but there are no time evidence items, so I shouldn't discuss time behaviour. I could mention that no time items qualified, but the instruction says not to discuss time when evidence contains no such items. I think mentioning that the time family produced no items is a screening fact, not a behavioural claim. To be safe, I'll keep focus on control flow. Actually, mentioning "no time items qualified" is fine as part of the screening comparison in the inference, but the Observed differences section should only describe behaviour from evidence items. Since there's one item, I'll describe it.

Observed differences section:
- The mix of A21's outgoing transitions shifted. Before, among A21's observed outgoing transitions, A23 took about 31 in 100 and A25 about 27 in 100, while A24 took about 17 in 100. In the later window, A24 took about 26 in 100, A23 about 21 in 100, and A25 about 20 in 100; smaller shares to A17 (3%→7%), A19 (13%→16.5%), A20 (0.5%→1.5%) also rose slightly. The overall dissimilarity was about 0.07 on the cosine scale, and the difference exceeded about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits of the pooled traces. Support: 200 outgoing transitions of A21 in each window. [DIR001]

Inference:
Support level: Insufficient evidence.
"The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process." Then one short sentence on limitation: screening expected about 0.29 control-flow items by chance and found one, which is what an unchanged process typically produces; a single routing indicator with high empirical strength cannot be distinguished from a sampling fluctuation.

Every bullet/paragraph stating a fact about data or hypothesis must end with exactly one pair of square brackets with evidence ids. The first line "Support level: Insufficient evidence" — is that a fact about the data? It's the required first line; I think it doesn't need a citation since it's the mandated format. The instruction says "Every bullet or paragraph that states a fact about the data or a hypothesis must end with exactly one pair of square brackets". The support level line is a judgement label, mandated verbatim. I'll leave it without brackets to keep it exact. Actually, to be safe, maybe the paragraphs after should have citations. The first line must be exactly "Support level: Insufficient evidence" — adding brackets would break exactness. I'll keep it plain.

Then: "The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process." — this is a conclusion; should it have a citation? It's about the evidence as a whole. I could cite [DIR001] since the whole inference rests on it. Hmm. The example in the instructions: "If the evidence list is empty, write only 'No inference can be made.' after the first line." That suggests the sentence itself doesn't carry citations. But the rule says every paragraph stating a fact about the data or hypothesis must end with brackets. The insufficiency statement is a judgement, not a fact about the data. I'll add a citation to the limitation sentence which does state facts (screening numbers). Let me structure:

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. The control-flow family produced one qualifying item where about 0.29 would be expected by chance in an unchanged process, so a single item of this size is what a stable process typically yields, and the one routing difference at A21 — however unusual it looks against random re-splits — cannot on its own rule out sampling variation [DIR001].

Hmm, that's one paragraph. Maybe split: first the insufficiency sentence, then a limitation sentence. The instruction: "You may add one short sentence on the limitation." So keep it to the required sentence plus one short limitation sentence.

Let me write:

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. Screening expected roughly 0.3 control-flow items by chance and found one, so a single routing difference at A21 — even one larger than about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits — is within what an unchanged process typically produces [DIR001].

That's concise. Good.

Observed differences — describe the DIR shift with both windows:

- The mix of successors chosen after A21 shifted. In the earlier window, among A21's observed outgoing transitions, roughly 31 in 100 went to A23 and 27 in 100 to A25, while A24 received about 17 in 100. In the later window, A24 received about 26 in 100, A23 about 21 in 100 and A25 about 20 in 100, with small rises for A17 (about 3 to 7 in 100), A19 (about 13 to 17 in 100) and A20 (under 2 in 100 in both windows). The overall profile difference was about 0.07 on the indicator's cosine scale and exceeded about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits, based on 200 observed outgoing transitions of A21 in each window [DIR001].

That's the only behavioural difference. No time or resource items, so don't discuss those.

Check citation rule: each bullet ends with exactly one bracket pair. Good.

Should I mention that these shares are over outgoing transitions, not cases? Yes, good to clarify for the reader.

Also note: "An empty profile or an unobserved edge does not show that an activity or edge is absent" — all eight successors appear in both windows, so no absence claims.

Final answer format: two sections.
